page.layout: One printed page of running text, with one note in the left margin beside the canon line "Regnum Congo Agages sive Jacchae destruxerunt." No right margin notes. Running head at top; page number 114 at top left; catchword "Aga-" at bottom right.

main_text.head: Explic.
main_text.p: Hoc regnum antiqvo & vero nomine appellatur Ambonda. Circa A. C. 1500 qvidam Æthiops nomine Angola, auxilio Lusitanorum, cæteros Regulos debellavit, & sese Monarcham constituit: a cujus nomine regio est Angola dicta. Huic ob rerum gestarum magnitudinem cognomen Ngenc[?], i e. Magnus, datum. Tanta hujus potentia fuit, ut 1000000. hominum in aciem perducere potuerit.
main_text.head: Periodus II. Canon.
main_text.p: destru-ctioRegnum Congo Agages sive Jacchæ destruxerunt.
main_text.head: Explicatio:
main_text.p: Occasio hujus calamitatis fuit fides Christiana, qvàm Reges Congo, svasu Lusitanorum, suscèperunt; & abalienatio Subditorum, & defectio provinciarum, secuta fuit. Tandem

page.notes: The word after "Ngenc" is in italic and hard to read; "Ngenc" is a doubtful reading (marked [?]). The numeral 1000000 is read from the scan as printed. The word "Agages" is italic and taken as printed. The catchword "Aga-" is in italic at the foot and is not repeated in the text. Faint show-through of the neighbouring page is ignored.
